story-context.title: AI Agent Panel Production Polish + User Preferences Architecture Foundation
story-context.overview: Two intertwined deliverables in one PR: (1) Polish the AI Agent panel for production: persist last prompt to DB (via existing aiAgentSettings.lastPrompt), add replace-form warning with "don't show again" preference, hide power-user controls (transport selector, retry input — backend defaults take over), silently autoload definitions even when soft validation issues are present. (2) Establish a User Preferences architecture foundation that mirrors the existing config.AppSetting pattern (UserPreference table + 2 ref tables + 3 endpoints + frontend Notifications section). The "don't show again" preference is the first consumer; all future preference-driven features plug into the same surface.

critical-objectives.item: The User Preferences architecture mirrors AppSetting and reuses ref.SettingType — no parallel type system.
Existing User.ThemePreferenceID / LayoutDensityID / FontSizeID / PreferredLanguageID / CountryID columns stay UNCHANGED. Migrating them is explicitly out of scope.
Default-value fallback semantics: when no UserPreference row exists for a user × key, return ref.UserPreferenceKey.DefaultValue. No backfill needed for existing users.
Frontend Notifications section dispatches controls dynamically by SettingType — adding a future preference must require zero frontend code changes for the ref-driven controls.
Last-prompt persistence reuses the existing aiAgentSettings.lastPrompt schema field from Story 6.3 — frontend wiring only, no backend schema change for this AC.
Retry default sourced from a new config.AppSetting row (form_ai.default_retries=2) — frontend stops sending the value at all.

Per Multi-Round UAT Protocol: 3 UAT rounds expected, single-variable per round. Round 1 = preferences foundation; Round 2 = AI panel polish ACs against the new prefs; Round 3 = catch-all + regression.

ac-group.label: AI Agent panel polish (the tactical layer)
ac-group.ac: Last prompt persistence — DB-backed via existing aiAgentSettings.lastPrompt; survives reload, switching forms, cross-device.
Replace-form warning — first time — modal containing words "replace" and "Undo" with Confirm/Cancel.
Replace-form warning — suppressed via UserPreference; survives logout/login; toggle in Notifications section restores warning.
Empty canvas — no warning regardless of preference state.
Outbound transport selector hidden; trace summary still shows resolved transport.
Retry input hidden; backend reads default from config.AppSetting form_ai.default_retries; updating row to 3 + reload causes 3 retries.
Silent autoload on soft validation issues — no banner/dialog; trace summary still shows counts.
Hard failure unchanged — definition-not-returned still surfaces existing failure message.

ac-group.label: User Preferences architecture (the foundational layer)
ac-group.ac: Three new tables exist with column shapes per §2.6.2; unique constraint on UserPreference (UserID + PreferenceKeyID); FK to existing ref.SettingType; standard audit columns matching User/AppSetting patterns.
GET /api/me/preferences returns prefs grouped by category with effective value (override OR default); brand-new user with no rows still sees all catalogue entries with DefaultValue.
PATCH /api/me/preferences accepts partial dict; validates each key against ref.UserPreferenceKey; transactional (no partial writes on validation failure); returns updated prefs.
DELETE /api/me/preferences/{key} removes the user's override row; next read returns DefaultValue.
Notifications section visible in Preferences UI; contains AI panel suppress-warning toggle; reads/writes via new endpoints; optimistic UI with rollback on error.

Default-value fallback works end-to-end — user who has never visited Notifications still sees default toggle state (warning enabled); modal shows on Generate over non-empty canvas; UserPreference row materializes on Confirm.

Future-extensibility demo — add a second demo preference (e.g. notifications.ai_agent.show_compile_summary) via ref seed only; Notifications UI auto-renders a control for it with no frontend code change. Proves SettingType-dispatch architecture genuinely scales.
docs/USER-PREFERENCES-ARCHITECTURE.md exists with schema, AppSetting comparison, 3-step recipe, fallback semantics, migration policy.

ac-group.ac: Bounded migration set: 6 expected (3 tables + 3 seeds), collapsible to ≤4 files. Any additional = scope-creep red flag.
